newsitem.title: CHINA: China sets Three Gorges bonds yield.
newsitem.headline: China sets Three Gorges bonds yield.

text.p: The maximum yield of the proposed one billion yuan ($120 million) bond issue to finance China's Three Gorges project would be 40 percent more than bank deposit interest rates, an official said on Monday.
The People's Bank of China, or central bank, was expected to approve the proposed issue next January or February, the official of the Yangtze Three Gorges Development Corp told Reuters by telephone.

China has poured 18 billion yuan ($2.17 billion) into the Three Gorges project which was scheduled to dam the Yangtze river next November, the Xinhua news agency quoted Yuan Guolin, assistant general manager of the company, as saying.
The Three Gorges -- the world's biggest water control project -- would need a total investment of $24 billion and 17 years to build, Yuan said.
The Three Gorges power plant would generate electricity by the year 2003, he said.
The project would break even by the year 2005 and all credits and interests would be paid off by 2009, he said.
